root_cause.text: A race in the LED class registration path exposed a `led_classdev` on `leds_list` before `led_init_core()` initialized its `set_brightness_work`, allowing trigger code to access and queue an uninitialized work item.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `list_add_tail(&led_cdev->node, &leds_list)` from before to after `led_init_core(led_cdev)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that `led_trigger_register()` could reach `led_set_brightness()` and queue the uninitialized `led_classdev.set_brightness_work` while the LED was already visible on `leds_list`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the global LED list insertion from this point in led_classdev_register_ext().
intent_record.what: The diff removes the block in led_classdev_register_ext() that acquires leds_list_lock, adds led_cdev->node to leds_list with list_add_tail(), and then releases the lock.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change stops the LED class device from being inserted into the global leds_list at that point in the registration flow, eliminating that specific list registration side effect from this location.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register new LED class devices in the global leds_list under lock so they are visible to LED list users.
intent_record.what: A new block was inserted after led_init_core(led_cdev) in led_classdev_register_ext() that acquires leds_list_lock with down_write(), adds led_cdev->node to leds_list using list_add_tail(), and then releases the lock with up_write().
intent_record.how: This makes each newly registered LED class device get inserted into the global LED list during registration under proper write locking, allowing later code that iterates or manages the registered LEDs through leds_list to see the device and preventing missing-list-registration behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by exposing the LED device on the global leds_list too early, before led_init_core() initializes set_brightness_work. Removing list insertion at that point directly addresses that premature exposure and the resulting race.

This change directly affects when a new LED class device is added to the global leds_list, which is the list involved in the race. Since the root cause is exposure of led_classdev on leds_list before led_init_core() initialized set_brightness_work, changing registration/visibility on leds_list is directly tied to the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This inserts the LED class device into the global leds_list before led_init_core() runs, making the object visible to trigger code that may access and queue the still-uninitialized set_brightness_work.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement publishes the LED class device on the global leds_list before led_init_core() has initialized set_brightness_work, creating a race where trigger code can find the device and queue an uninitialized work item.

Author: Richard Purdie <rpurdie@rpsys.net>
Date:   Fri Mar 31 02:31:04 2006 -0800

    [PATCH] LED: add LED class
    
    Add the foundations of a new LEDs subsystem.  This patch adds a class which
    presents LED devices within sysfs and allows their brightness to be
    controlled.
    
    Signed-off-by: Richard Purdie <rpurdie@rpsys.net>
    Cc: Russell King <rmk@arm.linux.org.uk>
    Cc: Greg KH <greg@kroah.com>
    Signed-off-by: Andrew Mor
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable registration ordering is visible directly in `led_classdev_register()`. The function creates the class device, sets devdata, creates sysfs attributes, and then exposes the LED globally via `list_add_tail(&led_cdev->node, &leds_list);`. There is no call to any initialization routine such as `led_init_core()` before adding the object to `leds_list`. Given the root cause, this means the `led_classdev` can become visible to trigger code before core fields like `set_brightness_work` are initialized. The fix would require initializing the core work item before the object is published on `leds_list`, but that handling is absent here. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not.
